content: The medication isavuconazonium sulfate is indicated for the treatment of invasive aspergillosis and invasive mucormycosis. It demonstrates activity against most strains of Aspergillus flavus, Aspergillus fumigatus, and Aspergillus niger in both in vitro studies and clinical infections. For invasive aspergillosis and mucormycosis, the recommended loading dose is 372 mg administered orally or intravenously every 8 hours for six doses (48 hours), followed by a maintenance dose of 372 mg once daily. In pediatric patients aged 1 year or older, isavuconazonium sulfate is also indicated for invasive aspergillosis or mucormycosis. However, its safety and efficacy have not been established in children under 1 year of age. Drug Interactions: 1. Contraindicated Medications: Certain drugs, such as amobarbital, apalutamide, atazanavir, bosentan, butabarbital, butalbital, carbamazepine, chloramphenicol, cobicistat, conivaptan, dabrafenib, darunavir, efavirenz, elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF, encorafenib, enzalutamide, etravirine, fosphenytoin, grapefruit, idelalisib, indinavir, itraconazole, ivosedinib, ketoconazole, levoketoconazole, lonafarnib, lopinavir, lumacaftor/ivacaftor, mifepristone, mitotane, nafcillin, nefazodone, nelfinavir, pentobarbital, phenobarbital, phenytoin, posaconazole, primidone, rifabutin, rifampin, rifapentine, rucaparib, St. John’s Wort, stiripentol, tipranavir, and voriconazole, are contraindicated due to their effects on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, which can either increase or decrease the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate. Avoid coadministration of these drugs. 2. Drugs Requiring Caution or Monitoring: Medications such as bosutinib, caplacizumab, dienogest/estradiol valerate, drospirenone, elacestrant, ethinyl estradiol, levonorgestrel, nirmatrelvir, pacritinib, repotrectinib, venetoclax, abatacept, acetaminophen, adalimumab, alefacept, alfentanil, alprazolam, amiodarone, amlodipine, anakinra, ansuvimab, antithymocyte globulin, apaziquone, aprepitant, armodafinil, atorvastatin, azathioprine, azelastine, basiliximab, belatacept, belzutifan, bendamustine, betamethasone, betrixaban, bicalutamide, bortezomib, brentuximab vedotin, brigatinib, brodalumab, bromocriptine, busulfan, calcitriol, canakinumab, capivasertib, carboplatin, carmustine, ceritinib, certolizumab pegol, chlorambucil, chlorzoxazone, cimetidine, ciprofloxacin, cisapride, cisplatin, clemastine, clobazam, clonidine, clotrimazole, cocaine (topical), colchicine, conjugated estrogens, corticotropin, cortisone, crizotinib, crofelemer, cyclophosphamide, cyclosporine, dacarabazine, daclizumab, danazol, daridorexant, darifenacin, dasatinib, deferasirox, deflazacort, desvenlafaxine, dexamethasone, dexlansoprazole, dexmethylphenidate, diazepam, diclofenac, dicloxacillin, digoxin, dihydroergotamine, and diltiazem may require dose adjustments or close monitoring due to their interactions with isavuconazonium sulfate. These interactions may involve changes in drug levels or effects, increased risk of toxicities, or reduced therapeutic efficacy. 3. Special Considerations: For drugs like omaveloxolone, dose adjustments are recommended if coadministration is unavoidable. For example, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. If adverse effects persist, further reduce the dose to 50 mg/day. For venetoclax, if a P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor for signs of toxicity. For betrixaban, reduce the dose to 80 mg orally once, followed by 40 mg orally daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. Mechanism of Interaction: Isavuconazonium sulfate is a substrate and inhibitor of CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein (P-gp). It can increase or decrease the levels of other drugs metabolized by these pathways, necessitating careful consideration of coadministration.
